summary: postinstall silently installs an undeclared sibling package into the installer's project
details: randompkga@1.0.11 ships no source code (no main entry, empty metadata) and its only effect on install is a postinstall hook `cd "$INIT_CWD" && npm i randompkgb`, which resolves and installs the unrelated, undeclared package `randompkgb` into the installer's own project directory. The pulled-in package is unpinned, so whatever version its publisher currently controls will be added to the installer's node_modules and executed when the installer's build or application runs. This is a dependency-chain pull-in primitive: installing randompkga causes attacker-selectable third-party code (randompkgb, at latest) to enter the installer's trust boundary at install time, with no declared purpose, no library functionality, and no way for the installer to see randompkgb in randompkga's package.json dependencies.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
